attributes.body:
かもしれない is an expression in Japanese that is often treated as a single word, but is actually the combination of the particle かも, and the potential form of the う-Verb 知（し）る (to know) with the auxiliary verb ない attached. かもしれない is regularly translated simply as 'might', or 'maybe', but the literal translation is much closer to 'even (A), we cannot know'.

To use かもしれない, attach it to the end of any verb, noun, な-Adjective or い-Adjective, in their non-polite (keigo) forms.

As the う-Verb 知（し）る is part of this construction, it may also be altered to its polite-potential form, creating かもしれません.

Due to かもしれない being such a common grammar pattern in daily speech for expressing uncertainty about various things, several colloquial forms also exist. These are かも, かもしらん, and かもしれん.

かも is by far the most common of these colloquial forms, with かもしらん potentially sounding a little bit rough/boyish.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Using 「かもしれない」 to express uncertainty

attributes.body: かもしれない and じゃないか can both appear at the end of a sentence, but differ in nuance. かもしれない expresses uncertainty, e.g. おいしいかもしれない ('It might be tasty.'). じゃないか is more emphatic and seeks agreement, e.g. おいしいじゃないか ('It's tasty, isn't it?' or 'I'm telling you it's tasty, don't you agree?').

おそらく and かもしれない both express possibility, but differ in certainty and placement. かもしれない comes at the end of sentences or phrases and means 'might' or 'may', e.g. 行くかもしれない ('I might go.'). おそらく appears at the beginning and expresses a stronger likelihood, e.g. おそらく行くだろう ('Most likely, I'll go.').

かもしれない (polite form かもしれません) and だろう (polite form でしょう) are both casual phrases used to express uncertainty or possibility, but with different degrees of certainty. かもしれない is less certain, similar to 'maybe' or 'might,' while だろう expresses a higher degree of certainty, like 'probably' or 'I guess.'

かもしれない (polite form かもしれません) and でしょう both express uncertainty or possibility, softening a statement. The main difference is the degree of certainty: かもしれない expresses less certainty, similar to 'maybe' or 'might,' while でしょう (casual だろう) expresses a higher degree of certainty, similar to 'probably' or 'I guess.'

かもしれない and もしかしたら both express possibility, but differ in placement and nuance. かもしれない appears at the end of sentences or phrases and means 'might' or 'may', e.g. 行くかもしれない ('I might go.'). もしかしたら comes at the beginning to emphasize the uncertainty, e.g. もしかしたら行くかもしれない ('Perhaps I might go.').
